scale.source: Swedish uses the long scale: CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-numbering: "1000000000: en miljard[ →→]", "1000000000000: en biljon[ →→]", "1000000000000000: en biljard[ →→]"

group_mark.source: CLDR 49.0.0 (unicode-org/cldr-json), cldr-numbers-full/main/sv/numbers.json, main.sv.numbers.symbols-numberSystem-latn: "group": " " (U+00A0, no-break space), "decimal": ",". A plain space between groups reads through space_groups.

decimal_mark.source: CLDR 49.0.0 (unicode-org/cldr-json), cldr-numbers-full/main/sv/numbers.json, main.sv.numbers.symbols-numberSystem-latn: "decimal": ",". Babel 2.18.0 gives the same: Locale.parse("sv").number_symbols["latn"]["decimal"] is ",".

space_groups.source: CLDR 49.0.0 (unicode-org/cldr-json), cldr-numbers-full/main/sv/numbers.json, main.sv.numbers.symbols-numberSystem-latn: "group": " " (U+00A0, no-break space). Babel 2.18.0 gives the same: Locale.parse("sv").number_symbols["latn"]["group"] is U+00A0. A plain space and U+202F also group digits, in any order.

compound_words.source: Swedish writes the words of a number below a thousand, and the thousands, as one word: CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-numbering: 21 → "tjugoett", 342 → "trehundrafyrtiotvå", 2500 → "tvåtusen femhundra"

plural_scale_needs_count.source: "miljoner" alone names no number: CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-numbering: "2000000: ←%spellout-cardinal-reale← miljoner[ →→]"

scale_noun_agrees.source: A count above one takes the plural: CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-numbering: "1000000: en miljon[ →→]", "2000000: ←%spellout-cardinal-reale← miljoner[ →→]"

joiner_tens_units.source: CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-numbering: "20: tjugo[→→]" ("tjugoett")

joiner_before_round_hundred.source: No joiner follows "tusen": CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-numbering: "1000: ←%%spellout-numbering-t←tusen[ →→]"

bare_hundred_after_scale.source: "hundra" names 100 alone, so after a group of thousands it starts the next group: "hundra" alone is 100 (SAOL; the page needs JavaScript, so not checked against the page); CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-numbering: "100: ←%spellout-numbering←hundra[→→]"

ten_joins_unit_ordinal.source: The ordinal 13th is one word, "trettonde", so "ten" and a unit ordinal are two numbers: CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-ordinal-masculine: 1 → "förste", 3 → "tredje", 4 → "fjärde", 5 → "femte", 6 → "sjätte", 7 → "sjunde", 8 → "åttonde", 9 → "nionde", 10 → "tionde", 11 → "elfte", 12 → "tolfte", 13 → "trettonde", 14 → "fjortonde", 15 → "femtonde", 16 → "sextonde", 17 → "sjuttonde", 18 → "artonde", 19 → "nittonde", 20 → "tjugonde", 30 → "trettionde", 40 → "fyrtionde", 50 → "femtionde", 60 → "sextionde", 70 → "sjuttionde", 80 → "åttionde", 90 → "nittionde"

ordinal_joiner_by_place.source: An ordinal takes the joiner that the cardinal word in its place takes. Between a ten and a unit (never): CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-numbering: "20: tjugo[→→]" ("tjugoett") After a hundred (never): CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-numbering: "100: ←%spellout-numbering←hundra[→→]"

comma_between_classes.source: CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-numbering: "1000: ←%%spellout-numbering-t←tusen[ →→]" writes no comma between two classes. No source opened shows a comma between two classes of one number, so a comma ends a number.

joiner_before_last_group.source: No joiner stands between groups: CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-numbering: "1000: ←%%spellout-numbering-t←tusen[ →→]"

one_before_ordinal_scale_is_fraction.source: A fraction is the ordinal and "-del" ("hundradel"), so a count of one before an ordinal scale word makes an ordinal: CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-ordinal-masculine: 100 → "etthundrade", 1000 → "ettusende", 1000000 → "en miljonte"

compound_shared_letter.source: "ettusen" is "et" + "tusen": CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-numbering: "1000: ←%%spellout-numbering-t←tusen[ →→]"; CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-numbering-t: "1: et". Svenska skrivregler: three equal consonants at a compound boundary are written as two (rule quoted from memory, not checked against the page)

ordinal_suffix_marks.source: CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %digits-ordinal-feminine: "0: =#,##0=$(ordinal,one{:a}other{:e})$"; CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %digits-ordinal-masculine: "0: =#,##0=:e"

joiner.source: "en och en halv" (SAOL; the page needs JavaScript, so not checked against the page); no joiner stands inside a Swedish number: CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-numbering: "20: tjugo[→→]"

decimal_marker.source: CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-numbering: "x.x: ←← komma →→"

minus.source: CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-numbering: "-x: minus →→"

minus_idioms.source: No Swedish idiom puts "minus" before a positive number.

number_noun.source: Wiktionary, "nummer", Swedish noun: "a number", "an item on a numbered list". The word after "nummer" names the number, so "nummer ett" is one, not the article.

article_one.source: "en" and "ett" are the indefinite article and the numeral 1: CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-cardinal-reale: "1: en"; CLDR RBNF sv (unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 data, sv.xml), %spellout-numbering: "1: ett"
